---
title: "Styling a Quarto Website with CSS/SCSS"
---

## Why Styling Matters to Your Readers

Consistent colors, fonts, and spacing make a site feel trustworthy and easy to read. Quarto lets me start from a built-in Bootstrap theme and then customize it.

## How I Applied It

In `_quarto.yml`, I combined a built-in theme with my own SCSS file:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
```

## The Two SCSS Sections

My `custom.scss` file has two sections:

1. `/*-- scss:defaults --*/` changes Bootstrap **variables**, such as the primary color and font.
2. `/*-- scss:rules --*/` adds **custom CSS rules** for specific classes.

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$primary: #1b6e5a;

/*-- scss:rules --*/
.skill-badge {
  background: $primary;
  color: white;
  border-radius: 999px;
}
```

## Using a Custom Class in a Page

Quarto's bracketed spans attach a CSS class to inline text. This is how the skill badges on my [home page](index.qmd) are styled:

```markdown
[Team Leadership]{.skill-badge}
```

## Live Example

::: {.hero}
This banner is styled by the `.hero` rule in my SCSS file.
:::

Here is the result: [Team Leadership]{.skill-badge} [Google Workspace]{.skill-badge}

## What I Learned

- Variables in `scss:defaults` change the whole site at once.
- Rules in `scss:rules` target individual elements.
- Using a variable like `$primary` in a rule keeps the design consistent.
